history.heading: Little Venice
paragraphs: Venezuela was home to Carib, Arawak and other indigenous peoples. In 1498 Columbus reached its coast. Explorers named it Venezuela, "Little Venice", after seeing indigenous houses on stilts over Lake Maracaibo. Spain established colonies, and cacao plantations used enslaved Africans.

history.heading: Independence
paragraphs: Venezuela was the first Spanish colony in South America to declare independence, in 1811. Simón Bolívar, born in Caracas, led the wars of liberation that freed Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Bolivia. Venezuela was part of Gran Colombia until 1830.

The 19th and early 20th centuries were dominated by caudillos (military strongmen), including Juan Vicente Gómez. Oil was discovered in the early 20th century, and by the 1920s Venezuela was one of the world's largest exporters.

history.heading: Democracy and chavismo
paragraphs: After the fall of dictator Marcos Pérez Jiménez in 1958, Venezuela became one of Latin America's most stable democracies, and it was a founding member of OPEC in 1960. Falling oil prices in the 1980s led to economic crisis and the deadly 1989 Caracazo riots.

Hugo Chávez, who led a failed coup in 1992, was elected president in 1998 and launched his "Bolivarian Revolution", using oil revenues for social programmes while concentrating power. After his death in 2013, Nicolás Maduro succeeded him. An economic collapse followed, with hyperinflation, shortages and the emigration of nearly 8 million people. Maduro's claimed victory in the 2024 election was widely disputed. In January 2026 a US military operation seized Maduro and took him to the United States to face charges.

culture.heading: Traditions
paragraphs: Spanish is the official language, and dozens of indigenous languages are recognised. Most Venezuelans are Catholic. Arepas, maize flatbreads with fillings, are a daily staple, and pabellón criollo is the national dish. Joropo is the national music and dance.

Baseball is the most popular sport, and many Venezuelans play in Major League Baseball. Venezuela has won many international beauty pageants. Angel Falls is the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall.

politics.heading: Political crisis
paragraphs: Venezuela has been governed by the United Socialist Party (PSUV) since 1999, with institutions such as the courts and electoral council under government control. The opposition, led by María Corina Machado, who won the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize, claims to have won the 2024 election. After Maduro's removal in 2026, the political situation remains in flux.

economy.heading: Oil and collapse
paragraphs: Venezuela has the world's largest proven oil reserves, and oil has long provided almost all export earnings. Mismanagement of the state oil company PDVSA, corruption, falling prices and US sanctions caused oil production and the economy to collapse after 2013, with GDP falling by around three-quarters.
Hyperinflation peaked at over a million percent in 2018. The economy partly stabilised through informal dollarisation. The currency is the bolívar.
